name: settings-form
description: An account settings page with a role dropdown, two switches, a slider and a theme choice. The forms step's pass mark: the registry has a select, a switch and a slider, so the agent should install and compose them instead of hand-building its own or using a native select. The theme choice should come from segmented or tabs.
prompt:
The home page of this app is still the Vite starter. Replace it with an account settings page for the studio site: the litt.design wordmark at the top, then a form. Name and email. A role, picked from a dropdown: Designer, Developer, Producer or Studio lead, with Designer selected. Two on/off switches: one for an email when a build finishes (on) and one for the weekly digest (off). A slider for the default animation speed, slower to faster, starting in the middle. A theme choice: light, dark or system, with system selected. Then a Save button at the bottom. Save can just show a quick confirmation on the page.

This is for litt.design, our own studio site, not a client job, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark, and on a phone.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the settings page as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide, full page), the role-open-* screenshots (after clicking the role control, 1440 wide) and the role-phone-* screenshots (after tapping the role control on a 390 wide touch screen). Claims:
1. page: this is a real account settings page, not the Vite starter: the litt.design wordmark at the top, then one left-aligned column with generous space and these controls in this order: name, email, role (showing Designer), two switches, an animation speed slider, a theme choice, and a Save button at the bottom. Nothing is missing.
2. page: every control has a visible text label (not only a placeholder), and the text inputs and the role control are roomy (about 44px tall) with only slightly rounded corners (about 6px).
3. page: each switch reads as on or off from its shape and not from color alone. The build-emails switch is on and the weekly digest switch is off, with the thumb at opposite ends of its track, and each switch has its label next to it. An on switch fills its track with the text color (near black in light, near white in dark), never the accent blue.
4. page: the slider has a track and a thumb about in the middle, and a clear direction (the words Slower and Faster, or the same idea, at the two ends). The thumb is a round mark clearly larger than the thickness of the track. The filled part of the track, if there is one, ends at the thumb and is the text color, not the accent blue.
5. page: the theme choice offers Light, Dark and System as one group of three options, with System marked as selected by a fill or a color and not by bold text. The selected option is visible in both the light and the dark screenshots.
6. role-open at 1440: the list is open and drawn on the page next to the role control. It shows Designer, Developer, Producer and Studio lead, with Designer marked as the current one (a check or a fill, not bold or a dot). It floats over the form without pushing the fields below it down, with a hairline edge, slightly rounded corners (about 10px) and a soft glow or shadow with no hard offset. A native browser select does not draw its list in a screenshot: if the role control is a native select, fail this claim and say native select in the reason.
7. role-phone at 390: the open list stays fully on the screen with no option cut off at an edge, and its rows are tall enough to tap (about 44px). If the role control is a native select, the screenshot cannot show its list: say native select in the reason and count this claim as passed.
8. All screenshots: Save is the only accent-filled button, all text is one even weight (nothing bold), there are no emoji, no decorative gradients and no hard offset shadows. The keyboard focus outline, the primary button's navy-to-cobalt fill (no glow) and the one soft light from the top (litt's light source, a faint tint that fades down a surface, once per view) are allowed. At 390 the form is one column and every control fits inside the screen. In the dark screenshots all text, the controls' edges and the switch states are clearly legible.
